subject: Deal prioritization: SLA bands & GPU allocation
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: laura@redwood.com, marcus@redwood.com, ben@redwood.com, monica@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Deal prioritization: SLA bands & GPU allocation

Team —

Putting this week’s fleet allocation ask on your radar. We’ve got a handful of near-term closes and a few large Q3 commitments that need explicit slot assignments so infra can schedule procurement or reserve burst capacity. I attached the latest forecast and an SLA band mapping (see attachments). High level:

- Nimbus Analytics (DEAL-4234): probability 65%, expected start Sept. Sales asks for 48 A100-equivalent reserved slots (~24k GPU hours/mo) to meet a 99.9% latency band.
- Acme pilot: smaller footprint but sensitive to latency during pilot window (Jul 15 start). Sales prefers 24 reserved-equivalent slots for pilot, but Acme may accept a lower SLA to reduce cost.
- Cloudscale integration: large batch inference, wants heavy burst capability (100 GPU burst) with a small dedicated commit.

Questions / asks:
1) Infra (Marcus): can you confirm procurement lead times and whether we can meet Sept start for Nimbus with a conservative procurement plan vs. burst fallback?
2) Finance (Laura): what’s the recommended tradeoff between committed slots and burst credits to keep ARR/unit economics intact?
3) Sales Ops (Ben/Monica): please confirm the minimum committed slot ask for each deal if we push for lower SLA bands.

Proposed temporary allocation (please comment):
- Nimbus: 36 reserved slots + 12 burst (contingent on quantization options)
- Acme: 12 reserved (pilot) + 12 burst; offer lower SLA band in pilot to cut cost by ~30%
- Cloudscale: 20 reserved + 100 burst credits for Q3 spikes

Please reply with firm numbers or objections by EOD Tuesday so I can lock this into the Q3 capacity plan and surface to the execs.

Attachments: [Attachment: 20270610_pipeline_mix_v2.xlsx] [Attachment: SLA_band_mapping.pdf]

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: priya@redwood.com, marcus@redwood.com, ben@redwood.com, monica@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 12:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal prioritization: SLA bands & GPU allocation

+1 on urgency. Quick finance read: the proposed mix above reduces short-term capital exposure but increases variable spend risk. A couple of notes:

- If we convert Nimbus to 48 committed slots we get a ~18% unit discount vs burst; finance prefers a slightly larger commit if the probability stays > 60%.
- For pilots (Acme), finance is comfortable with a pilot-level lower SLA if the customer signs a 6–9 month follow-on with a step-up to reserved capacity. We should capture that in the MAP/contract (HubSpot link below).
- Cloudscale: recommend structuring as a capped burst agreement (monthly cap) rather than open-ended burst credits — protects cost predictability.

Suggested revised allocation for planning discussion:
- Nimbus: 42 reserved + 6 burst (finance compromise)
- Acme: 8 reserved (pilot) + 16 burst; include a pilot-to-reserve clause in the MAP
- Cloudscale: 12 reserved + 100 burst (with monthly cap and overage penalty)

I added a quick burn projection in the attached sheet (see tab "Finance_Scenarios"). If we sign Nimbus at >65% probability, finance can latency-accelerate a capital request for Q3.

Related: https://hubspot.company/record/DEAL-4234

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Finance
laura@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: priya@redwood.com, laura@redwood.com, ben@redwood.com, monica@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal prioritization: SLA bands & GPU allocation

Thanks — a few infra constraints / options from my side:

- Procurement lead times for new A100-equivalent nodes are currently 10–12 weeks for delivery + 1–2 weeks to stage and test. If Nimbus needs full reserved capacity by September, we need a PO in the next 2–3 weeks.
- Current dedicated pool utilization is 82% in us-west; we have ~160 burst-capable GPUs available across zones but they are limited by cooling/electricity headroom in the facility; using burst beyond that requires fast-moving capacity or short-term cloud spot runs which increase cost and complexity.
- Technical mitigation: model quantization + KV caching can reduce required slot count for many real-time workloads. For instance, a 4-bit quantized variant plus caching cuts inferred slot demand for the recommended Nimbus model by ~30% in our bench. We should validate with the model team ASAP.

If Sales/Finance want to avoid a full 48-commit, we can do the following staged plan:
1) Start Nimbus with 30 reserved + 20 burst (burst paid by deal reserve credits)
2) Run a 6-week quantization pilot to reduce steady-state slot needs; if successful, convert 10 burst slots into reserved seats to stabilize pricing

I attached the infra runbook for dedicated burst provisioning — it lists gating checks we’ll need before we enable high burst across zones.

Attachments: [Attachment: infra_runbook_dedicated_burst.md]

Marcus Lin
Head of Infra Ops, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal prioritization: SLA bands & GPU allocation

Agree with Marcus and Laura. From a sales perspective we have some negotiating room on Nimbus if we pair the commit with a modest commercial concession (one-time onboarding credit or 2-month price guard). Two practical points:

- We should firm up the mapping of SLA band -> commercial credit now so AE/AMs have a clear playbook when customers ask for discounts during negotiation.
- For Cloudscale, converting to a smaller commit with a large burst buffer is acceptable if finance signs off on the capped-burst structure. I can draft the MAP language and the customer-facing quota table.

Proposed final planning numbers for this week’s call: (please approve or counter by EOD Mon)
- Nimbus (DEAL-4234): 36 reserved + 12 burst (sales credit: onboarding credit equivalent to 4 reserved slot months)
- Acme: 10 reserved + 14 burst; offer pilot 8-week lower-SLA option that converts to +20 reserved if they ramp
- Cloudscale: 15 reserved + 100 burst (monthly cap 1,200 GPU hours; overage at burst rate)

I’ll prepare the MAP language and update the HubSpot deal record once we confirm.

Ben Carter
Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
ben@redwood.com
